title: QuadraticFloorII: fibre sums and quartic traces at conductor 8lp
abstract: Sequel to QuadraticFloor. For an odd prime p, the alternating floor sums S_{A,B,C}(p) = sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p) with admissible (B, C) are averages of first Bernoulli numbers of the odd characters vartheta_{p,psi} = eta_p chi_{-4}^delta psi modulo 8Ap. The development proves that, weighted by psi_0(b)^2 and summed over the units b modulo A, these sums give minus the sum of B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}} over the fibre psi^2 = psi_0^2, which is real when psi_0^4 = 1; that for a prime l = 1 (mod 4), a quartic character xi modulo l and an odd prime p != l the real part of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}, Theta_{l,p} = vartheta_{p,xi}, and the Bernoulli number of eta_p (./l) are signed combinations of floor sums (the case l = 13 included); the Euler-factor relation B_{1,f 1_{l does not divide}}^{(ml)} = (1 - f(l)) B_{1,f}^{(m)} and the class-number shapes of the coefficients three and five; the quarter-range formula B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}}^{(8Ap)} = -sum_{0<x<=2Ap} vartheta_{p,psi}(x); and an elementary proof that both coordinates of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}^{(8lp)} are even integers, for every odd prime p. Every Bernoulli number is taken at a stated modulus; 8lp is the conductor of Theta_{l,p} only for p != l.
